```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tan_2026_fluorouracil"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tan_2026_fluorouracil"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-026-01645-1> (open access; the
  Electronic Supplementary Material holds the final NONMEM control stream)

Tan et al. first evaluated six published 5-FU population PK models against a
pooled Dutch dataset, found that none described it adequately (all
under-predicted the steady-state concentrations measured in gimeracil-stabilised
samples), and re-estimated a two-compartment model with Michaelis-Menten
elimination. Body surface area (BSA) was the only retained covariate, as a power
function on Vmax with an estimated exponent of 1.14. The final model was then
used to design limited sampling strategies and to propose BSA-based starting
doses (Table 3). This article packages the final model (Table 2 and the
supplementary control stream).

# Population

The model was fitted to 140 adults with gastrointestinal cancer from four
prospective Dutch cohort studies (CombiGaPP, PERFU, FUUT, FLOT; Table 1):
median age 63 years (IQR 56-70), 55% male, mean body weight 78.6 kg (SD 16.8),
mean BSA 1.94 m^2 (SD 0.25). Colorectal (42.1%) and pancreatic (34.3%) cancer
dominated, followed by gastric / gastro-oesophageal junction cancer (17.9%).
71.4% were DPYD wild type; the CombiGaPP study enrolled DPYD variant carriers
on genotype-guided reduced doses. Patients received FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, FOLFIRINOX
(bolus median 385 mg/m^2 plus a 46-48 h continuous infusion of median
2340 mg/m^2) or FLOT (24 h continuous infusion, no bolus). In total 435 5-FU
plasma concentrations (median 2 per patient, range 1-17) were available.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Tan_2026_fluorouracil")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lvc` (V1) | log(19.7 L) | Table 2 'V1 (L)'; ESM control stream THETA(3) |
| `lvp` (V2) | log(15 L) | Table 2 'V2 (L)'; ESM THETA(4) |
| `lq` (Q) | log(52.4 L/h) | Table 2 'Q (L/h)'; ESM THETA(5) |
| `lvmax` (TVVmax) | log(1900 mg/h) | Table 2 'TVVmax (mg/h)', defined at BSA 1.94 m^2; ESM THETA(6) |
| `lkm` (KM) | log(8.04 mg/L) | Table 2 'KM (mg/L)'; ESM THETA(7) |
| `e_bsa_vmax` (EXPO) | 1.14 | Table 2 'EXPO'; ESM THETA(8) |
| `etalvmax` | 0.10 (variance) | Table 2 'ETA_Vmax' (omega^2); ESM `$OMEGA` |
| `propSd` | 0.34 | Table 2 'Proportional error (%)' 34%; ESM THETA(1) |
| `addSd` | 0.0001 mg/L, fixed | ESM THETA(2) '(0.0001) FIX ; additive error' |
| `vmax = TVVmax * (BSA/1.94)^EXPO * exp(eta)` | n/a | Table 2 Vmax row: `Vmax = TVVmax * (BSA/1.94)^EXPO * exp(ETA_Vmax)`; ESM `$PK` |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | ESM `$DES`: `DADT(1) = -C1*VM/(KM + C1) + K21*A(2) - K12*A(1)`, `DADT(2) = K12*A(1) - K21*A(2)` |
| `d/dt(auc_central) <- Cc` | n/a | ESM `$DES`: `DADT(3) = C1` (AUC compartment) |
| Residual error | combined | ESM `$ERROR`: `W = SQRT(PROPER**2*IPRED**2 + ADDER**2)` with `$SIGMA 1 FIX` |

# Virtual cohort and regimens

The paper's dose-finding simulations (Table 3, Figure 5) resampled BSA from the
140 modelling patients. Those data are not public, so BSA is drawn here from a
normal distribution with the Table 1 mean and SD (1.94 +/- 0.25 m^2), truncated
to 1.4-2.6 m^2. Doses are given per m^2 and converted to mg with each subject's
BSA. The four regimens of Table 3 are simulated with 200 subjects each.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20260521)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260521)

n_per_arm <- 200
bolus_dur <- 5 / 60 # 5-min bolus (Figure 1 sampling scheme)
ci_dur <- 46 # 46-h continuous infusion

regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~bolus_mgm2, ~ci_mgm2,
  "CI 2400", 0, 2400,
  "CI 2800", 0, 2800,
  "Bolus 200 + CI 2400", 200, 2400,
  "Bolus 400 + CI 2400", 400, 2400
) |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimen))

obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  0, 0.05, bolus_dur, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6,
  8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 30, 36, 40, 44,
  bolus_dur + ci_dur + c(0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12)
)))

make_arm <- function(arm, id_offset) {
  subj <- tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n_per_arm),
    BSA = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_per_arm, 1.94, 0.25), 1.4), 2.6),
    regimen = regimens$regimen[arm]
  )
  bolus <- subj |>
    filter(regimens$bolus_mgm2[arm] > 0) |>
    mutate(
      time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
      amt = regimens$bolus_mgm2[arm] * BSA, rate = amt / bolus_dur
    )
  # The continuous infusion starts when the bolus ends (Figure 1); without a
  # bolus it starts at the same clock time so both regimens share one grid.
  ci <- subj |>
    mutate(
      time = bolus_dur, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
      amt = regimens$ci_mgm2[arm] * BSA, rate = amt / ci_dur
    )
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0, rate = 0)
  bind_rows(bolus, ci, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  make_arm(i, id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[events$evid == 0, c("id", "time")]))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Tan_2026_fluorouracil")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("regimen", "BSA"),
  maxsteps = 1e6
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

## Figure 5: concentration-time profiles

```{r figure-5, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
sim |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    Q50 = median(Cc),
    Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(time <= bolus_dur + ci_dur) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of 5-FU administration (h)",
    y = "5-FU plasma concentration (mg/L)",
    title = "Median and 90% prediction interval",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Tan 2026 (dashed line at 0.8 mg/L as in panels c-d)."
  )
```

The bolus regimens peak at the end of the 5-minute bolus and fall within about
an hour to the infusion plateau; the infusion-only regimens rise to a plateau
of roughly 0.4-0.6 mg/L within 1-2 h, the shape shown in Figure 5.

## Table 3: median AUC0-inf and target attainment

AUC0-inf is read from the `auc_central` accumulator at the last record, 12 h
after the end of the infusion, by which time the concentration is negligible
(the low-concentration elimination rate constant is about
(Vmax/Km)/V1 = 12 h^-1).

```{r table-3}
auc_sim <- sim |>
  group_by(id, regimen) |>
  slice_max(time, n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(id, regimen, BSA, auc = auc_central)

table3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~pub_median, ~pub_p05, ~pub_p95, ~pub_in, ~pub_below, ~pub_above,
  "CI 2400", 21, 12, 36, 42, 45, 13,
  "CI 2800", 25, 14, 43, 49, 25, 26,
  "Bolus 200 + CI 2400", 24, 14, 41, 48, 29, 23,
  "Bolus 400 + CI 2400", 29, 17, 50, 41, 13, 45
)

auc_summary <- auc_sim |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    sim_median = median(auc),
    sim_p05 = quantile(auc, 0.05),
    sim_p95 = quantile(auc, 0.95),
    sim_in = 100 * mean(auc >= 20 & auc <= 30),
    sim_below = 100 * mean(auc < 20),
    sim_above = 100 * mean(auc > 30),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(regimen = as.character(regimen)) |>
  left_join(table3, by = "regimen") |>
  mutate(pct_diff_median = 100 * (sim_median / pub_median - 1))

auc_summary |>
  transmute(
    regimen,
    median = sprintf("%.1f [%.0f-%.0f]", sim_median, sim_p05, sim_p95),
    published = sprintf("%d [%d-%d]", pub_median, pub_p05, pub_p95),
    in_target = sprintf("%.0f (%d)", sim_in, pub_in),
    below = sprintf("%.0f (%d)", sim_below, pub_below),
    above = sprintf("%.0f (%d)", sim_above, pub_above)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen (mg/m^2)" = regimen,
    "Simulated AUC0-inf median [5-95%] (mg*h/L)" = median,
    "Table 3 AUC0-inf median [5-95%] (mg*h/L)" = published,
    "20-30 mg*h/L, % sim (Table 3)" = in_target,
    "< 20, % sim (Table 3)" = below,
    "> 30, % sim (Table 3)" = above
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated vs. published AUC0-inf (Table 3 of Tan 2026).")
```

```{r table-3-check}
# The regimen medians are the structural check: a mis-transcribed Vmax, Km,
# BSA exponent or dose conversion moves every median by tens of percent. The
# Monte-Carlo SE of a 200-subject median with ~30% CV is about 3%, and the
# published medians are rounded to whole mg*h/L (up to +/- 2.5% at 21), so
# 10% leaves several SEs of headroom on any cohort.
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_summary$pct_diff_median) < 10))
```

## Typical-value check over the full dose grid (Table S6)

Because AUC is monotone in the single random effect (eta on Vmax), the
population median AUC at a given BSA equals the AUC of the subject with
eta = 0. The typical-value AUC at the median BSA (1.94 m^2) therefore
approximates the Table S6 medians for every regimen the authors simulated,
without Monte-Carlo noise.

```{r table-s6}
s6 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~bolus_mgm2, ~ci_mgm2, ~pub_median,
  0, 2100, 17, 0, 2200, 19, 0, 2300, 20, 0, 2400, 21, 0, 2500, 22,
  0, 2600, 23, 0, 2700, 24, 0, 2800, 25, 0, 2900, 26, 0, 3000, 27,
  200, 2000, 19, 200, 2200, 22, 200, 2400, 24, 200, 2600, 25, 200, 2800, 27,
  300, 2000, 23, 300, 2200, 24, 300, 2400, 26, 300, 2600, 28, 300, 2800, 30,
  400, 2000, 26, 400, 2200, 27, 400, 2400, 29, 400, 2600, 31, 400, 2800, 33
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), BSA = 1.94)

ev_s6 <- bind_rows(
  s6 |>
    filter(bolus_mgm2 > 0) |>
    transmute(id, BSA, time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
              amt = bolus_mgm2 * BSA, rate = amt / bolus_dur),
  s6 |>
    transmute(id, BSA, time = bolus_dur, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
              amt = ci_mgm2 * BSA, rate = amt / ci_dur),
  s6 |>
    transmute(id, BSA, time = bolus_dur + ci_dur + 12, evid = 0L,
              cmt = "central", amt = 0, rate = 0)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

mod_typical <- mod |> rxode2::zeroRe()

# zeroRe() removes the random effects on purpose; rxode2 warns on every
# multi-subject solve without omega, so muffle that one warning only.
solve_typical <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

typ_s6 <- solve_typical(mod_typical, events = ev_s6, maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  select(id, auc_typical = auc_central) |>
  left_join(s6, by = "id") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc_typical / pub_median - 1))

typ_s6 |>
  transmute(
    regimen = ifelse(bolus_mgm2 > 0,
                     paste0(bolus_mgm2, " + ", ci_mgm2),
                     paste0("CI ", ci_mgm2)),
    auc_typical = round(auc_typical, 1),
    pub_median,
    pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen (mg/m^2)" = regimen,
    "Typical-value AUC0-inf, BSA 1.94 (mg*h/L)" = auc_typical,
    "Table S6 median (mg*h/L)" = pub_median,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value AUC0-inf vs. Table S6 population medians.")

# Deterministic: the only slack is the whole-number rounding of Table S6
# (up to 3% at 17 mg*h/L) and the spread of BSA around 1.94 in the authors'
# resampled cohort.
stopifnot(abs(median(typ_s6$pct_diff)) < 5, max(abs(typ_s6$pct_diff)) < 10)
```

## Steady-state closed form

During the infusion-only regimen the plateau must satisfy the Michaelis-Menten
mass balance R = Vmax * Css / (Km + Css), i.e. Css = Km * R / (Vmax - R),
where R is the infusion rate. This checks the elimination term independently
of the published simulations.

```{r ss-check}
ev_ss <- tibble(
  id = 1:3, BSA = c(1.6, 1.94, 2.3)
) |>
  mutate(amt = 2400 * BSA, rate = amt / ci_dur)
ev_ss <- bind_rows(
  ev_ss |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  ev_ss |> mutate(time = 40, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0, rate = 0)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

ss <- solve_typical(mod_typical, events = ev_ss, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  select(id, Cc) |>
  left_join(ev_ss |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, BSA, rate), by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    vmax_i = 1900 * (BSA / 1.94)^1.14,
    css_closed = 8.04 * rate / (vmax_i - rate),
    rel_err = Cc / css_closed - 1
  )
knitr::kable(
  ss |> select(BSA, Cc, css_closed, rel_err) |>
    dplyr::rename("Simulated Cc at 40 h (mg/L)" = Cc,
                  "Closed-form Css (mg/L)" = css_closed,
                  "Relative error" = rel_err),
  digits = c(2, 4, 4, 6)
)
# Same parameters on both sides; 40 h is > 100 distribution half-lives, so the
# difference is integration error only (measured ~1e-9).
stopifnot(all(abs(ss$rel_err) < 1e-4))
```

## Table S4: median AUC0-inf by BSA stratum

Table S4 reports median AUC0-inf within four BSA strata. The typical-value
AUC at a representative BSA for each stratum (1.5, 1.7, 1.9 and 2.1 m^2) is
shown beside it for three regimens.

```{r table-s4}
s4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~bolus_mgm2, ~ci_mgm2, ~BSA, ~pub_median,
  0, 2400, 1.5, 20.3, 0, 2400, 1.7, 20.9, 0, 2400, 1.9, 21.7, 0, 2400, 2.1, 22.4,
  200, 2400, 1.5, 24.6, 200, 2400, 1.7, 23.7, 200, 2400, 1.9, 23.5, 200, 2400, 2.1, 23.0,
  400, 2400, 1.5, 29.4, 400, 2400, 1.7, 28.7, 400, 2400, 1.9, 28.9, 400, 2400, 2.1, 28.7
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())

ev_s4 <- bind_rows(
  s4 |>
    filter(bolus_mgm2 > 0) |>
    transmute(id, BSA, time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
              amt = bolus_mgm2 * BSA, rate = amt / bolus_dur),
  s4 |>
    transmute(id, BSA, time = bolus_dur, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
              amt = ci_mgm2 * BSA, rate = amt / ci_dur),
  s4 |>
    transmute(id, BSA, time = bolus_dur + ci_dur + 12, evid = 0L,
              cmt = "central", amt = 0, rate = 0)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

typ_s4 <- solve_typical(mod_typical, events = ev_s4, maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  select(id, auc_typical = auc_central) |>
  left_join(s4, by = "id")

typ_s4 |>
  transmute(
    regimen = ifelse(bolus_mgm2 > 0,
                     paste0(bolus_mgm2, " + ", ci_mgm2),
                     paste0("CI ", ci_mgm2)),
    BSA,
    auc_typical = round(auc_typical, 1),
    pub_median
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen (mg/m^2)" = regimen,
    "BSA (m^2)" = BSA,
    "Typical-value AUC0-inf (mg*h/L)" = auc_typical,
    "Table S4 median (mg*h/L)" = pub_median
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value AUC0-inf by BSA vs. Table S4 of Tan 2026.")
```

For the bolus regimens the model and Table S4 agree in level and trend. For the
infusion-only regimen the levels agree (about 20-22 mg*h/L) but Table S4 shows
AUC rising with BSA while the model, as published in Table 2 and the control
stream, gives a slight fall (see Assumptions and deviations). This row set is
shown for transparency and is not used as a pass/fail gate.

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA computes Cmax and AUC0-inf for each simulated subject. The 5-FU
concentrations after the end of the infusion fall by many orders of magnitude
within hours, so the numerically-zero tail is dropped before the half-life fit.

```{r pknca}
stopifnot(all(sim$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim$Cc), na.rm = TRUE))
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  filter(time <= time[which.max(Cc)] | Cc >= 1e-4 * max(Cc)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(id, time, Cc, regimen)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  group_by(id, regimen) |>
  summarise(time = 0, amt = sum(amt), .groups = "drop")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published_nca <- table3 |>
  transmute(regimen, aucinf.obs = pub_median)

nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "regimen",
  params = "aucinf.obs",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PKNCA AUC0-inf (median) vs. Table 3 of Tan 2026. * differs by >20%.")
```

```{r pknca-vs-accumulator}
# The trapezoidal PKNCA AUC and the model's integrated AUC must agree; the
# residual is the trapezoid error on the coarse sampling grid around the bolus
# peak (largest for the 400 mg/m^2 bolus).
pk_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  select(id, regimen, aucinf = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(auc_sim |> select(id, auc), by = "id") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (aucinf / auc - 1))
stopifnot(abs(median(pk_auc$pct)) < 5, quantile(abs(pk_auc$pct), 0.9) < 10)
```

All four regimen medians agree with Table 3 within the rounding of the
published values, and the target-attainment fractions follow the same pattern:
the standard 400 + 2400 mg/m^2 regimen puts close to half of the population
above 30 mg*h/L, while infusion-only 2400 mg/m^2 leaves close to half below
20 mg*h/L.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **BSA distribution.** The authors resampled BSA from their 140 patients; the
  individual data are not public, so BSA is drawn from a normal distribution
  with the Table 1 mean and SD (1.94 +/- 0.25 m^2), truncated to 1.4-2.6 m^2.
  The BSA formula (DuBois, Mosteller, ...) is not stated in the paper.
- **Bolus duration and infusion start.** The paper does not state the bolus
  duration used in the dose-finding simulations. A 5-minute bolus is assumed
  from the Figure 1 sampling scheme (bolus from 0 to 5 min) and the
  'end of bolus' sampling times of 0.08-0.1 h in Table S5; the 46-h continuous
  infusion starts when the bolus ends.
- **Additive residual error.** Table 2 reports only the proportional error
  (34%). The control stream also carries an additive error fixed at
  0.0001 mg/L, combined with the proportional term as
  sqrt(prop^2 * IPRED^2 + add^2); it is kept, fixed, so the residual model
  matches the fitted one. It is negligible against the 50 ng/mL lower limit of
  the assays.
- **AUC compartment.** The authors added an AUC compartment (`DADT(3) = C1`)
  to their control stream to obtain the reference AUC0-inf; it is carried as
  the `auc_central` state.
- **Covariates not retained.** Total body weight, sex, DPYD gene activity
  score, age, creatinine and eGFR were explored (stepwise covariate modelling)
  but only BSA was retained, so no other covariate enters the model. Inter-
  occasion variability on Vmax (12%) and study-, centre- and assay-specific
  effects were tested and not retained; IIV on V1 was dropped for >50%
  shrinkage.
- **Table S4 by BSA stratum.** For the infusion-only rows, Table S4 shows the
  median AUC0-inf rising with BSA (e.g. 20.3 to 22.4 mg*h/L at
  2400 mg/m^2), whereas for the bolus rows it falls with BSA. With the
  per-m^2 dose scaled linearly with BSA and Vmax scaled by BSA^1.14, the
  published model predicts a slight fall with BSA for both regimens (the
  steady-state concentration is Km * R / (Vmax - R), and R / Vmax falls as
  BSA^-0.14). The packaged model follows Table 2 and the control stream; the
  infusion-only stratum-level Table S4 values are therefore shown but not used
  as a validation target. The pooled medians (Table 3, Table S6) and the bolus
  rows of Table S4 are reproduced.
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article (Europe PMC,
  checked 2026-11-14).
